about: CMT's closed list (DESIGN.md section 7). Every study here is screened by its design documents and accounted for in data/cases.json, either cased or set aside with a reason; no study is added after the freeze except the frozen search's hits, committed in data/search.json before any case. Every bibliographic detail and every recollection of a design below is from memory, not checked. The recollections say why a study is listed and what its screen is expected to find; the screen decides, not these notes.

studies.cite: Battalio, Samuelson and Van Huyck 2001, 'Optimization incentives and coordination failure in laboratory stag hunt games', Econometrica 69(3)
studies.recalled: three stag hunts sharing one mixed equilibrium, random matching within cohorts over many rounds; my recollection is that the safe action's payoff depends on the partner there, which item (b) would exclude

studies.cite: Cooper, DeJong, Forsythe and Ross 1992, 'Communication in coordination games', Quarterly Journal of Economics 107(2)
studies.recalled: a two-action coordination game in which one action pays the same against either action; a no-communication baseline with rematching; payoffs in lottery points

studies.cite: Cooper, DeJong, Forsythe and Ross 1990, 'Selection criteria in coordination games: some experimental results', American Economic Review 80(1)
studies.recalled: mostly games of three actions, which item (a) would exclude

studies.cite: Straub 1995, 'Risk dominance and coordination failures in static games', Quarterly Review of Economics and Finance 35(4)
studies.recalled: several two-action coordination games with rematching

studies.cite: Clark, Kay and Sefton 2001, 'When are Nash equilibria self-enforcing? An experimental analysis', International Journal of Game Theory 29(4)
studies.recalled: two-action coordination games with and without messages

studies.cite: Schmidt, Shupp, Walker and Ostrom 2003, 'Playing safe in coordination games: the roles of risk dominance, payoff dominance, and history of play', Games and Economic Behavior 42(2)
studies.recalled: two-action coordination games varying risk and payoff dominance, random and fixed matching treatments

studies.cite: Rydval and Ortmann 2005, 'Loss avoidance as selection principle: evidence from simple stag-hunt games', Economics Letters 88(1)
studies.recalled: stag hunts some with negative payoffs

studies.cite: Feltovich, Iwasaki and Oda 2012, 'Payoff levels, loss avoidance, and equilibrium selection in games with multiple equilibria: an experimental study', Economic Inquiry 50(4)
studies.recalled: stag hunts whose payoffs differ by a constant added to every cell: candidates for the shift pairs

studies.cite: Dubois, Willinger and Van Nguyen 2012, 'Optimization incentive and relative riskiness in experimental stag-hunt games', International Journal of Game Theory 41(2)
studies.recalled: stag hunts varying the optimization premium and riskiness, repeated play

studies.cite: Dal Bo, Frechette and Kim 2021, 'The determinants of efficient behavior in coordination games', Games and Economic Behavior 130
studies.recalled: many stag hunts with random rematching across sessions; replication files may be public

studies.cite: Buyukboyaci 2014, 'Risk attitudes and the stag-hunt game', Economics Letters 124(3)
studies.recalled: stag hunts with measured risk attitudes

studies.cite: Friedman 1996, 'Equilibrium in evolutionary games: some experimental results', Economic Journal 106(434)
studies.recalled: two-action games, coordination games among them, under random pairwise and mean matching in groups over many periods

studies.cite: Cheung and Friedman 1997, 'Individual learning in normal form games: some laboratory results', Games and Economic Behavior 19(1)
studies.recalled: two-action games, coordination games among them, random pairwise and mean matching

studies.cite: Rankin, Van Huyck and Battalio 2000, 'Strategic similarity and emergent conventions: evidence from similar stag hunt games', Games and Economic Behavior 32(2)
studies.recalled: payoffs drawn anew each round, which item (d) would exclude

studies.cite: Van Huyck, Battalio and Beil 1990, 'Tacit coordination games, strategic uncertainty, and coordination failure', American Economic Review 80(1)
studies.recalled: a minimum-effort game of seven actions with a group-level payoff, which item (a) would exclude

studies.cite: Al-Ubaydli, Jones and Weel 2013, 'Patience, cognitive skill and coordination in the repeated stag hunt', Journal of Neuroscience, Psychology, and Economics 6(2)
studies.recalled: fixed partners, which item (c) would exclude

studies.cite: Belloc, Bilancini, Boncinelli and D'Alessandro 2019, 'Intuition and deliberation in the stag hunt game', Scientific Reports 9
studies.recalled: one-shot play, which item (g) would exclude

studies.cite: Centola, Becker, Brackbill and Baronchelli 2018, 'Experimental evidence for tipping points in social convention', Science 360
studies.recalled: a naming game with a committed minority and a partner-dependent payoff for the status quo, which items (b) and (e) would exclude; listed as the out-of-class case

studies.cite: Andreoni, Nikiforakis and Siegenthaler 2021, 'Predicting social tipping and norm change in controlled experiments', PNAS 118(16)
studies.recalled: thresholds measured and distributed across members; expected to fail (b) or (a)

search.about: Run once, on Ren's yes, before any screen; its hits are written to data/search.json and committed once, after the freeze and before data/codings.json, data/layout.json and data/cases.json are committed (cmt_rule.closed_list checks the order and refuses a second commit of any of the four; cmt_rule.run refuses a search not committed after the freeze). The archives and their query forms are from memory, not checked.
archives: openICPSR (the AEA data and code repository)
search.query: the exact phrase "stag hunt" in the title, description or keywords
search.cutoff: deposits public on or before 5 November 2026
search.hit: a deposit holding data of a laboratory or online experiment, written in search.json's 'hits' as {"id", "deposit", "title"}; a deposit of a study already listed above goes under 'already listed' with that study's id, not among the hits, and adds nothing
search.cap: if more than 150 deposits match, every one is still listed in search.json and screened; the cap is only the spend guard of DESIGN.md section 12

coding_form.about: What each deciding coder records from a study's design documents alone (instructions, payoff tables, protocol), with every result, figure and data file withheld. One form per game a study ran; the two forms must be identical for the game to be admitted.
coding_form.status_quo: the action whose payoff is the coded HS and HH: the action that is not the payoff-dominant equilibrium's; where the game has none, the action whose payoff varies less with the partner
coding_form.payoff: SS, SH, HS, HH: the row player's payoff in the experiment's own units, S the other action, H the status quo; exactly as the table gives it
coding_form.two_actions_symmetric: true where each member chooses one of two actions each round and the payoff table is the same for both members of a pair
coding_form.matching: 'random pairs' (partners drawn anew each round within the matching group), 'mean matching' (payoff against the group's average), 'fixed partners' or 'other'
coding_form.independent_groups: true where members of different matching groups never meet
coding_form.constant_parameters: true where the payoff table, the group and the rules do not change over the rounds of the game
coding_form.committed_members: true where any member is a confederate, a programmed player or one whose action is fixed
coding_form.communication: true where members can send messages, or the round has another stage (punishment, voting, a second game)
coding_form.first_game_of_group: true where this game is the first the group plays in the session
coding_form.feedback_own_payoff: true where each member learns at least the own payoff after each round
coding_form.group_size: members in a matching group, as the design sets it
coding_form.shift_of: the game_id of a game of the same study whose every payoff differs from this one's by one constant, or null
